L44: # CATALOG
L45: 【20†The CEDEJ library, which the Center partly inherited from the French School of Law in Cairo, holds around 36,000 volumes and 6,500 maps. CEDEJ has resumed a policy of new acquisitions in the Humanities and Social Sciences concerning Egypt and Sudan since 2025. The library welcomes all researchers and students to its Garden City reading room.
L46: In addition to its physical collections, the library offers access to several digital archives, including a fully searchable Egyptian press archive.†cedej.bibalex.org】 CEDEJ also published nearly 300 books and booklets since its creation, some of which were digitized and are accessible 【32†here†books.openedition.org】.

L2: 【0†Access ARCE's Library Portal >>>†library.arce.org】
L3: 
L4: ### The ARCE Library will be closed from September 1 through November 30 in preparation for its relocation. Limited access may be possible by appointment. Please contact 【1†[email protected]】 or 【2†[email protected]】 to inquire about availability.
L5: 
L6: ### 【3†Image】
L7: ### ARCE’s Library
L8: 
L9: ARCE established its scholarly library in 1978 to support research on various aspects of the history and culture of Egypt. Today the collection contains more than forty thousand volumes, of which approximately 20 percent are in Arabic.
L10: 
L11: #### 【4†Explore the Library’s Floor Plan >>】
L12: #### Collections
L13: 
L14: 【5†Image】
L15: The library collection focuses on Egyptology and Islamic studies and includes most standard scholarly reference works as well as some 300 journal titles. The acquisition is undertaken on other subject areas (e.g. Greco-Roman World, Arabic Literature).
L16: The Simpson Library collection also includes a substantial number of rare books, including a complete set of the bulletins of the Comité de Conservation des Monuments de l’Art Arabe, a first edition of the Description de l’Egypte (one of only five complete sets in Egypt), and the catalogues généraux of the Egyptian Museum and the Musée National de l’Art Arabe (the present-day Islamic Museum).
L17: 【6†Image】
L18: 
L19: A unique feature of the Simpson Library is the photocopied collection of select Arabic manuscripts that are held in various Middle East Libraries. Acquired by scholars working in Cairo and throughout the Middle East over the past eighty years, the collection includes many works by the Arabic philosopher Avicenna and members of his school. These works have been photocopied for public use; the originals are preserved in acid-free paper.
L20: #### Users
L21: 
L22: 【7†Image】
L23: The Simpson library is available to ARCE members, staff, fellows and representatives of affiliated expeditions. It is also accessible to the staff of the Supreme Council of Antiquities, faculty at Egyptian universities and postgraduate students, members of other foreign institutes and expeditions and, by courtesy, to colleagues in general. The library’s large volume of publications in western languages, especially English, makes it an invaluable resource to scholars in the Cairo area.
L24: ######
L25: #### ARCE’s Library Portal
L26: 
L27: In 2021,  ARCE launched its new Library Portal, designed to expand access to our collections and better serve the research community.
L28: 
L29: ARCE Members now have full access to:
L30: 
L31:   * Our online catalog
L32:   * The ARCE Digital Library, which already includes more than 5,000 e-books
L33:   * Subscription databases, including Brill, Archaeopress, and JSTOR
L34: 
L35: Non-members may browse the online catalog and access all open-access publications linked through the portal.
L36: The digital library will continue to grow through new database subscriptions and the acquisition of additional e-publications, ensuring that ARCE remains a leading resource for Egyptologists, archaeologists, and heritage professionals worldwide.
L37: 
L38: Access the library portal 【0†here.†library.arce.org】
L39: ######
L40: #### Photocopying & Scanning Services
L41: 
L42: ARCE members and registered graduate student users who have a letter from their supervisors may request photocopies or scans of articles. They may also request one chapter per book and up to 10% of a book. Scans will be emailed to the requester after the payment is made. Users must send an email to 【8†[email protected]】 to schedule payment and photocopy pickup time.
